title: Time of Maximum Interval Overlap
statement:
You are given `n` closed intervals `[start[i], end[i]]` on an integer time line, for example the arrival and departure times of guests at a party. An interval covers time `t` when `start[i] ≤ t ≤ end[i]`, so both endpoints count: a guest who leaves at time `5` and a guest who arrives at time `5` are present together at time `5`.

Find the integer time `t` at which the **largest number of intervals overlap**. If several times reach the same maximum, report the **smallest** such time.

Print that time and the number of intervals covering it.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `start[i]` and `end[i]`.
outputFormat: Print two space-separated integers: the earliest time with maximum overlap, and the number of intervals covering it.

examples.explanation: Time 1 is covered by one interval. From time 2 to time 4 both [1, 4] and [2, 5] are active, so the maximum is 2 and its earliest time is 2. [9, 12] never overlaps another interval.
The endpoints are inclusive, so at time 3 both [1, 3] and [3, 6] are active. Time 5 also has two intervals, but 3 is earlier. No time has all three.
A single point interval covers only time 5.

hints: Checking every interval against every candidate time is O(n^2). The overlap count only changes at interval endpoints, so think of the intervals as events along the time line.
Create +1 events at each start and -1 events just after each end (at end + 1, since the end is inclusive), sort the events by time, and sweep while keeping a running count.
Apply all events that share the same time before reading the count, and only record a new best when the count is strictly larger so that the earliest time is kept.
